title: Put the key in a combination key safe and lock it
instruction: Put the key in the key safe and lock it.
context: Done by: maids and housekeepers, property managers and personal care aides (O*NET 37-2012, 11-9141, 31-1122) leaving keys at changeovers. A shut combination key safe is not locked until its wheels are turned off the code; one left on its code opens for anyone. The instruction does not state this. Unlike TK-AR39QP (set wheels to a code to open a box) and TK-93MYCS (lock a door, then post its key), here the code must be scrambled, and only after the lid is shut.
setup: Directions are from the robot's view; 'in front' means away from the arm bases, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Key safe (fixed to the table, grey painted steel): a box 126 mm deep, 92 mm wide, 50 mm tall, centred on the midline, its front face 217 mm in front of the arm bases. The front 48 mm is a solid strip holding three black number wheels; behind it is the key compartment, 72 mm front to back, 80 mm wide, 45 mm deep (floor 5 mm thick, walls 6 mm). Each wheel is black plastic, 40 mm across, 10 mm thick and 20 g, turning up to 178 degrees either way about a left-right axis 12 mm below the top and 22 mm behind the front face; the wheels are 25 mm apart (one on the midline, one each side), 8 mm of rim stands above the top, and each has a white index tooth 10 x 10 mm standing 12 mm proud of its rim. Each wheel clicks in 36-degree steps (ten numbers): a spring of 0.15 N m/rad pulls it to the nearest step, so a wheel pushed past 18 degrees goes on to the next number. The code is every tooth pointing straight up, and all three start there. Lid: a light grey steel plate 78 mm front to back, 92 mm wide, 8 mm thick, 0.10 kg, hinged along the box's back top edge, opening up to 110 degrees; a stiff hinge (3 N m/rad, giving 0.02 rad) holds it where it is left. Mechanism: while every wheel is on the code the lid opens and shuts freely; with a wheel off the code and the lid shut, the lid is locked; with a wheel off the code and the lid open, a bolt stands out and stops the lid 9 degrees short of shut; a lid already below 9 degrees when the wheel is turned is stopped where it is (but never below 3.1 degrees). The bolt stays out until every wheel is back on the code. Key (loose, 30 g, rigid): a red plastic fob 22 mm front to back, 20 mm wide, 22 mm tall, with a brass blade 24 x 12 x 3 mm along its bottom edge pointing away from the robot. Lot A: the lid stands open 109 degrees (leaning back past upright) and the key lies on the table 235 mm in front of the arm bases and 170 mm left of the midline (fob centre). Lot B: lid open 90 degrees; key 335 mm in front, 150 mm left. Lot C: lid open 100 degrees; key 160 mm in front, 90 mm left. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end, with both grippers more than 5 mm from the key, the lid and every wheel, and everything still. 1.0: every corner of the key is inside the compartment (within its inner outline and below the rim), the lid is shut to within 2 degrees, and at least one wheel is turned off the code: its white tooth no longer points up, 18 degrees (half a number) or more from straight up; success must hold for 1 s. Every other outcome scores 0: the lid shut with every wheel still on the code, the lid held open by the bolt because a wheel was turned first, the key outside the safe or on top of it, or anything still held or moving. There is no partial credit: a shut safe on its code is open to anyone. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Turn every wheel back to the code (teeth up), take the key out, set it at the lot's place and open the lid to the lot's angle (A 109, B 90, C 100 degrees). Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: The safe is fixed to the table with its lid on top, like a portable key box; wall-mounted safes have a front door. The bolt is a stop on the lid hinge that moves with the wheel positions. Wheels click in 36-degree steps and carry no numbers; the code is shown by the teeth. The key is two boxes. The lots move the key and the lid angle, so a single fixed script fails; a replay of all three layouts could pass.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C; in lot A the left arm reached the key and moved it a little on the table but never lifted it; the lid stayed open and no wheel turned); demo: 1.0 in each lot
